title: Evaluating Generate–Validate–Repair Pipelines for Intent‑to‑Configuration NetOps Tasks: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study that isolates downstream validator/repair effects under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Using a 1000‑task synthetic NetOps stress corpus (2000 paired episodes) and a deterministic digital‑twin validator, we compared a baseline single‑shot LLM configuration generator against a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline (with a canary stage). Declared model: gpt‑5‑mini (provider: openai_responses); validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics exactly one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by both arms; only deterministic validation and the permitted single repair call could create paired outcome differences. Observed outcomes: baseline safe‑deploy = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded safe‑deploy = 1000/1000 = 1.000; paired difference = 0.005 (n11=995, n10=5, n01=0, n00=0). The preregistered primary inferential test (exact two‑sided McNemar) yields p = 0.0625 (not < 0.05). The preregistered paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) is [0.001, 0.01]. Only five validator‑triggered repairs occurred and total model calls used = 1005 (shared_initial = 1000; repair = 5). We report the exact McNemar as the preregistered confirmatory outcome, present the bootstrap CI as a secondary descriptive summary, label any one‑sided McNemar as exploratory/post‑hoc, and interpret the small absolute guarded benefit in light of sparse discordant counts, high baseline validity, validator scope, and the shared_initial_candidate design.

sections.introduction:
Automating intent→configuration translation for network operations can reduce manual effort but raises safety risks: multi‑step sequencing errors, transient invariant violations, and protected‑field interference can convert plausible command sequences into harmful actions. Prior surveys and controlled studies document LLM hallucination, prompt sensitivity, and structured‑output failures that affect code and configuration generation, motivating architectures that pair generative models with deterministic validators and bounded repair procedures [1],[2].

This paper reports a preregistered, artifact‑grounded paired experiment (cand‑003‑stud‑001) that isolates purely downstream validator/repair effects under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Our research question: when baseline and guarded conditions begin from the exact same sampled initial candidate (shared_initial_candidate), to what degree can a downstream deterministic validator plus a single allowed repair call (guarded pipeline with a canary stage) improve paired safe‑deploy outcomes compared with reusing the same initial candidate unmodified (baseline)? The design intentionally isolates downstream interventions so any paired difference is attributable to validation and permitted repair only.

Contributions. (1) A preregistered paired experiment (Npairs = 1000) with deterministic task selection from the challenging_workflow_stress_v1 corpus and archived validator traces. (2) Full execution accounting and artifact grounding (completed pairs = 1000; hosted_model_call_event_count = 1005; repair calls = 5; declared model = gpt‑5‑mini; execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset — null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0). (3) Transparent reporting of the preregistered confirmatory test (exact two‑sided McNemar; p = 0.0625), preregistered descriptive summaries (paired bootstrap CI = [0.001, 0.01], bootstrap_seed = 1729), and explicit labeling of post‑hoc explorations.
sections.related_work:
Surveys and empirical studies document hallucinations, prompt sensitivity, and structured‑output failures that reduce correctness for code and configuration tasks; these motivate verifier‑assisted architectures [1],[2]. Constrained decoding and schema‑aware planning reduce syntactic/executable errors in structured domains, though much evidence originates outside NetOps and depends on validator fidelity when applied to networking [3]. Recent NetOps and agentic‑AI system work emphasizes verifier‑assisted repair, guarded architectures, and protocol‑mediated governance as mitigations; these works provide prototypes and argue that operational reliability depends on validator coverage and enforced protocols rather than on any single model alone [4],[5],[6].

Our preregistered paired design complements prior work by isolating downstream validation/repair effects under shared_initial_candidate semantics; it therefore does not measure prompt or decoding interventions that would require independent first‑pass generations.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and frozen design. The preregistration (cand‑003‑stud‑001) was frozen prior to any hosted‑model invocation (preregistration_sha256 recorded in the execution manifest = ab4c6436c6ece56bf47da7730d50485a17cdb9bb86a90a4231042303d3b489ec). Key preregistered elements: paired binary design; task_count = 1000 deterministic tasks from the challenging_workflow_stress_v1 corpus; generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate; initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; primary test = exact two‑sided McNemar. Secondary preregistered summaries: paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729) and sensitivity analyses treating failed calls as unsafe.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and interpretation. Under shared_initial_candidate both baseline and guarded episodes begin from the same sampled initial candidate; the guarded pipeline may reject the candidate via deterministic validation and may invoke at most one permitted repair call. Thus paired outcome differences can only arise from deterministic validator decisions and permitted repair(s); the design does not measure effects from independent first‑pass generation changes or constrained decoding arms that were not executed.

Model and validator. Declared model: gpt‑5‑mini (provider: openai_responses); archived model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset (explicitly not evidence of deterministic hosted‑model sampling). Orchestration adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1; validator/digital twin: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator enforces workflow policies, required command presence/order, protected‑field noninterference and returns a deterministic binary safe‑deploy verdict per task manifest). The validator's rule coverage is a construct whose limitations are discussed below.

Task corpus and selection. Tasks were selected deterministically using the preregistered ordinal rule to produce exactly 1000 unique tasks. Each task manifest contains initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and difficulty labels (very_hard, extreme). The deterministic validator compares parsed candidate sequences to manifest constraints and emits structured validator traces archived per episode.

Execution accounting and missingness. The preregistration limited retries (maximum_attempts_per_call = 1). The execution manifest records completed_episode_count = 2000, failed_episode_count = 0, hosted_model_call_event_count = 1005, and stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation = 1000, repair = 5}. The analysis executor applied the preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' missingness treatment; preregistered sensitivity analyses treating failures as unsafe were available but not required because failed episodes = 0.
sections.results:
Execution and primary outcomes. The run completed with planned episodes = 2000, completed = 2000, and complete_pairs = 1000. The paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is n11 = 995 (both succeeded), n10 = 5 (guarded succeeded, baseline failed), n01 = 0 (baseline succeeded, guarded failed), n00 = 0 (both failed). Observed success rates: baseline = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded = 1000/1000 = 1.000; observed paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar returns p = 0.0625; this does not meet the preregistered two‑sided α = 0.05 threshold, so preregistered H1 is not supported.

Preregistered secondary summaries and repair outcomes. The paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) yields [0.001, 0.01] as a preregistered descriptive summary. Only five validator‑triggered repairs occurred (repair stage_count = 5); representative archived episode artifacts show validator rejection for required_sequence violations or protected_interface touches, a single allowed repair call, and acceptance of the repaired candidate after revalidation. Total model calls used = 1005 (shared_initial = 1000; repair = 5). Contamination checks, exclusions, and missingness applied zero post‑hoc exclusions; missingness_summary.csv records zero failed or unscorable episodes.

Clarifying the inferential hierarchy (prerequisite reviewer request). The preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar test is the confirmatory analysis and it did not reach two‑sided α = 0.05 (p = 0.0625). The paired bootstrap CI and any one‑sided McNemar reported are descriptive/exploratory and do not overturn the preregistered confirmatory null. The bootstrap CI can exclude zero despite the nonsignificant exact two‑sided McNemar because bootstrap percentile intervals with extremely sparse discordant counts (here n10=5, n01=0) produce a discrete empirical distribution of paired differences; the percentile bounds therefore reflect resampling variability over the small number of discordant events rather than increased confirmatory power. This behavior and the exact n11/n10/n01/n00 counts are archived in analysis artifacts.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Since baseline and guarded reused the same initial candidate, only deterministic validation and the permitted single repair could create paired differences. The five observed repairs illustrate that a validator with adequate coverage can correct some ordering/sequence violations. However, the low repair invocation count constrains general conclusions: it may reflect few initial candidate violations in the synthetic corpus, generator behavior for the declared model+prompt, or limited validator scope. Distinguishing among these requires follow‑ups varying generator semantics, repair budgets, and validator rule sets.

Power assumptions and limitations. The preregistered power plan assumed baseline ≈ 0.60 and a target absolute increase of 0.15; the observed baseline (0.995) substantially departs from that assumption and produces very few discordant pairs, limiting sensitivity of the exact paired test. Thus the nonsignificant two‑sided McNemar does not imply absence of any practical guarded benefit in contexts with higher baseline failure prevalence.

Threats to validity. Construct validity depends on validator rule coverage: omitted policy checks would inflate measured success. Internal validity benefits from deterministic seeding and zero failed episodes; however, shared_initial_candidate semantics intentionally preclude measuring first‑pass generation interventions. External validity is limited by the synthetic corpus, a single model (gpt‑5‑mini), and the deterministic validator; generalization to heterogeneous production environments is not established. Conclusion validity is constrained by sparse discordant counts and the resulting discrete inferential behavior.

Operational implications and recommended preregistered follow‑ups. Artifact‑grounded evidence shows verifier‑guided repair can avert some unsafe outcomes in synthetic workflow settings, but marginal gains depend on baseline failure prevalence, validator sensitivity/coverage, and permitted repair budget. Preregistered follow‑ups we recommend and archive support: (1) evaluate independent first‑pass generation arms (no shared_initial_candidate) to measure prompt/decoding intervention effects; (2) sweep repair budgets (0..k repairs) to quantify marginal returns per failure class; (3) expand validator rule suites and topology heterogeneity to probe external validity; (4) include multiple model families to map model dependence. Each follow‑up should align power calculations to plausible baseline failure rates and preregister analysis choices.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered paired study with shared_initial_candidate semantics on a 1000‑task synthetic NetOps stress corpus, a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline produced a small absolute paired improvement (0.005) relative to a baseline single‑shot generator; the preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar test did not reach α = 0.05 (p = 0.0625). Only five validator repairs were invoked and total model calls used = 1005. The primary inferential outcome is the preregistered exact McNemar result; any one‑sided McNemar is explicitly labeled exploratory because it was not prespecified. These artifact‑grounded results indicate that downstream verifier/repair safeguards can prevent some unsafe outcomes, but measurable marginal gains are constrained when baseline outputs are already highly valid and when the paired design isolates downstream effects. Full preregistration, execution manifests, raw responses, validator traces, and analysis artifacts are archived with the run to support reproducibility and to guide preregistered follow‑ups that broaden model diversity, validator coverage, and repair budgets.

Preregistration: cand‑003‑stud‑001 (frozen prior to any model calls). Immutable initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). After the autonomy lock, literature review, preregistration finalization, execution, analysis, manuscript drafting, autonomous peer review, and automated revisions were performed by the autonomous research run; no human manually edited the manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Single‑model scope: only the declared model gpt‑5‑mini was evaluated; results do not generalize across model families or versions.

Synthetic corpus and deterministic validator: tasks come from a synthetic stress corpus and validation used a deterministic digital twin (deterministic_netops_validator_v5); external validity to heterogeneous vendor/legacy environments is limited.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: the paired comparison isolates downstream validator/repair effects only; it does not measure differences that would arise from independent first‑pass generations or alternative prompting arms that were not executed.

Low baseline failure prevalence: baseline success = 99.5%; the preregistered power plan assumed baseline≈0.60 and a target effect of 0.15, so the observed baseline greatly reduces sensitivity to detect small absolute gains under the preregistered confirmatory test.
Sparse repairs and interpretation limits: only five validator repairs were invoked, constraining inference about repair efficacy across failure modes.

Statistical nuance: the preregistered primary test is exact two‑sided McNemar (p = 0.0625). The paired bootstrap percentile CI [0.001, 0.01] is a preregistered descriptive summary but is sensitive to sparse discordant counts; a one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) was computed post‑hoc and is explicitly labeled exploratory because it was not prespecified.

Construct validity: the safe‑deploy binary depends on the emulator/validator's rule set; semantic and emergent multi‑device policy violations may be underrepresented in the validator's modeled constraints.
